correctness.rationale: Direct planar radial-cone integration gives A=ab∫_0^1(a²+b²t²)^((q-2)/2)dt and its transpose; derivative of log R has sign(q-2) by two strict pointwise comparisons. Convergence at r→0,∞ gives exact attainable mass-ratio intervals, and the B equation fixes the unique scale. All convex-body realizers have four coordinate normal facets and hence are rectangles. For q>=1, the opposite-facet mass function has H′(s)=∫(s²+y²)^((q-4)/2)[(q-1)s²+y²]dy>0, forcing central symmetry without an a priori symmetry assumption. For 0<q<1 the same mass function on [-1,1] tends to zero at both ends and is positive inside, producing two unequal opposite supports with equal mass; the centered inverse provides a distinct second solution of the same even measure. The q=2 fiber is ab=A. A no-dependency checker verified 228 finite cases, including independent angular/radial integrals, polynomial identities, inverse recovery, and asymmetric witnesses; proof is analytic and not inferred from finite tests.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Xiong–Yang prove uniqueness for even q<2 only within origin-symmetric convex bodies, not arbitrary realizers not symmetric about the origin, and exhibit q>2 nonuniqueness for other even measures. Böröczky et al and Shan give stronger abstract symmetric existence conditions for q<2; the resulting low-q symmetric image is covered, not counted as novel. Necessary higher-q concentration bounds imply some ratio obstructions but do not prove existence and full fibers for four atoms; no checked theorem implies the sharp global symmetry threshold.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is the full four-normal even-data image and explicit reconstruction for q>2, global rigidity of all realizers about the origin for q>=1, and an exact symmetry-breaking threshold with nonsymmetric witnesses for every 0<q<1. Existing 2017/2019 and 2026 symmetric subspace concentration theorems already imply the abstract even symmetric image for q<2, and Xiong–Yang already establish uniqueness among symmetric bodies there; these known components are expressly excluded from the originality basis. The complete global four-atom fibers for q>2 and origin-symmetry threshold are not consequences of the checked sources: they require new sharp support-number and cone-integral arguments. Published mathematical-record and earlier theorem comparisons were done by implications, not titles. Priority risk of unindexed older treatments remains.
residual_risks: Older discrete planar logarithmic and dual Minkowski literature, including work on rectangular support functions, could independently contain an equivalent four-normal formula or off-center symmetry-breaking mechanism.
The q<2 symmetric existence and uniqueness components are prior-covered; novelty depends on the global origin-symmetry rigidity/threshold and q>2 explicit sufficiency/fibers.
External literature searches and records are incomplete; original priority has not been independently certified.

value.rationale: The inverse of the four-atom dual curvature measure is a natural minimal non-general-position Minkowski problem. A complete sharp all-q realizability and reconstruction provides useful exact boundary examples, while the fully non-symmetric inverse is rigid for q>=1 despite known q>2 nonuniqueness for other data. The explicit q<1 non-centered witnesses expose a genuine symmetry-breaking phase transition at q=1. These are motivated structural and complete natural classification facts rather than isolated unmotivated arithmetic or a normalization check; q<2 previously known symmetric existence/uniqueness is not counted as value supplied by this result.
